## Check your understanding

For additional practice outside the lesson, see the [exercise space — mathematical foundations](../exercises.qmd#foundations).

1. Why does the cross-entropy derivative with respect to logits simplify to $p_i-\mathbb{1}[i=y]$?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

For a one-hot target, differentiating log-softmax combines the normalization term $p_i$ with the target-class term $-\mathbb{1}[i=y]$. Their difference is the gradient with respect to each logit.

</details>

2. What can disagreement between an analytical gradient and a finite difference indicate?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

It may indicate a derivation or implementation bug, but also a poorly chosen $\epsilon$, rounding error, nondeterministic behavior, or mismatched conventions. Isolate the case and check tolerances.

</details>

3. Why might a gradient-descent update fail to reduce the loss if the step is too large?

<details>
<summary>Show answer</summary>

The gradient describes a local change. A step that is too large can leave the region where that approximation is useful, overshoot a minimum, or increase the objective; the learning rate must be controlled.

</details>
